description:
### Summary

* Registry-artifact-based Google Drive mounting point detection

  * [x] Add method for reading Google Drive registry artifacts and parsing them as JSON.

  * [x] Add method for safely traversing the resulting JSON and creating/returning new CloudProvider objects based on the data inside.

  * [x] Call these methods after the old approach that uses the "root_preference_sqlite" file. Google Drive now appears under Cloud Drives" in the sidebar regardless of whether it is mounted as a drive or a folder.

* GoogleDriveCloudDetector private fields

  * [x] Add private fields to GoogleDriveCloudDetector (GDCD) for the strings used to access/traverse Google Drive registry artifacts.

  * [x] Add field to GDCD for the logger service so we can log warnings when artifact access/traversal attempts fail.

* Icon-file-getting logic

  * [x] Create method for getting the icon file so we can reuse this logic.

  * [x] Improve null safety of icon file getting logic.

### Resolved / Related Issues

* https://github.com/files-community/Files/issues/15698

### Steps used to test these changes

1. Under Google Drive Preferences -> Settings -> Google Drive Streaming Location, choose "Folder" or "Drive Letter".

    1. Folder

        1. I opened Files and looked at the sidebar and "Google Drive" was there under "Cloud Drives".

        2. I clicked on "Google Drive" and it opened my drive with all its contents viewable and accessible, as expected. I opened a few of my files (images and pdfs) and they opened as expected.

    2. Drive Letter

        1. I opened Files and looked at the sidebar and "Google Drive" was there under "Cloud Drives".

        2. I clicked on "Google Drive" and it opened my drive with all its contents viewable and accessible, as expected. I opened a few of my files (images and pdfs) and they opened as expected.

2. I also found that everything worked exactly the same if I had the entire old approach that uses the "root_preference_sqlite" file commented out. However, I did not want to commit it in this state because my testing was not especially thorough, but it might be worth looking into whether this will work now entirely without the old approach.

@wharvex is this required here? We've been working to remove the Vanara package so hopefully we can find an alternative API.

Ah okay, thanks for letting me know. I used that because I needed to get the target of a shortcut. When syncing is set to mirror, the "My Drive" folder in the streaming location is a shortcut, so I needed to get its target path for the CloudProvider SyncFolder. I tried to find how shortcut targets usually get resolved in the repo, and I could only find examples that used Vanara. I used `Files.App.Utils.Shell.ShellFolderExtensions.GetShellItemFromPathOrPIDL` which returns a Vanara `ShellItem`.

I'm working on an alternate method for getting the target (without dependencies), based on the approach I found [here](https://stackoverflow.com/a/77142277/16458003). I got a prototype working in a separate repo, I'm just cleaning it up and then I'll test it out in my Files fork. I'm hoping to make a push in the next couple days. Or let me know if you already have another preferred method of getting shortcut targets that does not use Vanara.

> Or let me know if you already have another preferred method of getting shortcut targets that does not use Vanara.

You're trying to enumerate inner items in a IShellItem (a folder).

I'm working on removing Vanara, to support NativeAOT when WinAppSdk 1.6 available (Vanara contains ComWrappers which isn't compatible with IL Trimming and NativeAOT)
The replacement is CsWin32, generator of P/Invokes (this is compatible with it). 

However there's an issue with CsWin32, where it emits COM interfaces with methods that return void instead of HRESULT. But this can be resolved by not allowing marshaling in CsWin32's config file. We should be able to do that but currently blocked by #15834 (I'm removing it because it collides with our CsWin32 config and bc of package size reduction).

---

The conclusion is that you can use it for now. I'll replace it later (with IWindowsShellService.Enumerate() I guess).
I appreciate if you append a comment in the right above as:
`// TODO: Avoid to use Vanara (#15000)`

Thanks!

Okay no problem, I'll add that comment. And yes, just to clarify, in `AddMyDriveToPathAndValidate` I get an IShellItem for the streaming location and cast it to a ShellFolder, which allows me to get its contents as ShellItems. I then get "My Drive" from these items as a ShellLink and get its `TargetPath` property, which is what I ultimately needed. Unfortunately it's a little hard to follow in the code because I had to do it all in one line or else it gave me an exception that said something like "COM object that has been separated from its underlying RCW cannot be used."
